comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Rights and Depositary Share Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, except for Series B and Series L which lack early redemption rights. Ownership is generally held via depositary shares representing fractional interests in preferred stock, with dividend payment frequencies and minimum rates varying by series as detailed in the table footnotes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America utilize depositary shares to represent fractional interests in their perpetual preferred stock series, noting that dividends are payable if and when declared. Citigroup's Series Z uses depositary shares representing a 1/25th interest. Bank of America's disclosure indicates that ownership of most preferred series is held in depositary shares representing fractional interests (e.g., 1/1,000th, 1/25th, or 1/1,200th depending on the series), with dividends payable quarterly or semi-annually as declared.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs disclose the issuance of Series Z preferred stock with fixed-rate reset dividend structures and depositary share representations. Citigroup's Series Z pays quarterly fixed dividends until May 15, 2028, resetting to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.209%, represented by 1/25th interest depositary shares. In contrast, Goldman Sachs issued its Series Z in January 2025 with a higher fixed rate of 6.85% until February 10, 2030, resetting to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.461%, also represented by 25 depositary shares per share (1/25th interest) but paying semi-annual dividends.

sentences.text: (11)Issued as depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of the corresponding series of non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock.

Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, May 15, 2028, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series Z reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.209%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.
In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock (Series Z Preferred Stock).

Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.

comparisons.peer_topic: Preferred Stock Dividend Policy and Reference Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: Dividends are discretionary, non-cumulative, and declared quarterly. Fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock uses SOFR or CMT as reference rates following the transition from LIBOR, with specific spread adjustments defined.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase disclose preferred stock dividend structures that transition from a fixed rate to a floating rate based on a treasury benchmark. Citigroup's Series Z resets to the five-year treasury rate plus a spread after a fixed period. Similarly, JPMorgan Chase notes that its fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock uses the five-year Constant Maturity Treasury (CMT) rate plus spreads as the reference rate after the fixed period, with dividends declared quarterly and non-cumulative.

sentences.text: Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, May 15, 2028, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series Z reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.209%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.
References to "CMT" mean a floating annualized rate equal to the five-year Constant Maturity Treasury ("CMT") rate plus the spreads noted.
Dividends are payable quarterly on fixed-rate preferred stock.
